aiOverview.content: The 3-hour rule in China is a 2021 regulation limiting minors (under 18) to only three hours of online gaming per week. Enforced by the National Press and Publication Administration, this policy restricts play to 8 p.m.–9 p.m. on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays, aiming to curb addiction and promote physical health. Key details of the policy include: Time Limit: A maximum of 3 hours per week. Approved Times: Only 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and public holidays. Enforcement: Game companies must use real-name verification (and often face recognition) to ensure children cannot play outside these times, as reported by Al Jazeera and Reuters. Al Jazeera Reuters Scope: Applies to online gaming, though some studies show young gamers occasionally try to bypass it using adult IDs, says Medium and Reddit users. Medium Reddit users Background and Impact Context: The rules are a response to concerns about gaming addiction, which state media once termed "spiritual opium". Prior Rules: It tightened 2019 restrictions, which allowed 90 minutes on weekdays and 3 hours on weekends. Impact on Companies: Companies like Tencent and NetEase reported a decline in revenue from minors. Tencent Industry Changes: According to Niko Partners, the number of youth gamers fell from 122 million in 2020 to 82.6 million in 2022, though some recovery is predicted. Niko Partners
